module_title: Compass Survey, Bearings, and Local Attraction
introduction: This level tackles angular measurements. Questions here focus heavily on converting Bearings, identifying Local Attraction, and calculating Magnetic Declination numericals.

core_concepts.title: WCB and QB (Bearing Systems)
core_concepts.description:
1. **Whole Circle Bearing (WCB):** The angle is always measured from the North in a clockwise direction ($0^{\circ}$ to $360^{\circ}$). It is measured using a **Prismatic Compass**.
2. **Quadrantal Bearing (QB / Reduced Bearing):** The angle is measured from the North or South (whichever is closer) toward the East or West ($0^{\circ}$ to $90^{\circ}$). E.g., $N 30^{\circ} E$. It is measured using a **Surveyor's Compass**.

core_concepts.title: Fore Bearing (FB) and Back Bearing (BB)
core_concepts.description:
The bearing of a line in the direction of the survey progress is the Fore Bearing, and in the opposite direction is the Back Bearing. 
Formula: **$\text{BB} = \text{FB} \pm 180^{\circ}$** 
(Use $+$ if FB is less than $180^{\circ}$, and $-$ if FB is greater than $180^{\circ}$).

core_concepts.title: Local Attraction
core_concepts.description:
The deviation of a magnetic needle from its true North due to the presence of local magnetic objects (e.g., steel structures, electric wires, iron ore). 
**Identification Rule:** If the difference between the Fore Bearing (FB) and Back Bearing (BB) of a line is exactly **$180^{\circ}$** ($|\text{FB} - \text{BB}| = 180^{\circ}$), both stations are considered completely free from local attraction.

important_entities.name: Magnetic Declination
important_entities.key_fact: The Angle between True North and Magnetic North
important_entities.significance:
The horizontal angle between the true meridian and the magnetic meridian. 
Formula: **True Bearing = Magnetic Bearing $\pm$ Declination** 
[Use $+$ for Eastern Declination, and $-$ for Western Declination].

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation:
The Hardest Exam Trap: Students constantly confuse these two. 
- **Declination:** A horizontal angle that changes with geographic location. 
- **Dip:** The vertical angle of inclination of the magnetic needle from the horizontal. The value of Dip is **$0^{\circ}$ at the Equator** and **$90^{\circ}$ at the Magnetic Poles**.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Because a magnetic needle aligns vertically at the magnetic poles, the dip angle is perfectly $90^{\circ}$.

exam_strategy_tips: NUMERICAL ALERT: If the FB of a line is $60^{\circ}$, what is its BB? Answer: $60^{\circ} + 180^{\circ} = 240^{\circ}$.
